correctness.rationale: Unit row norms and determinant 70 checked exactly; 9, 9 and 1 independent two-subset paths give the claimed polynomial risks. Every chosen maximal residual is strictly maximal across t in [1/2,3/2]; the 22 quadratic margins are proven positive by exact vertex tests. The two polynomial risk gaps have explicitly positive numerators over the full interval. One-step minimality is from a nested uniform-permutation coupling and the orthogonal projection identity, not a finite experiment.

value.rationale: The example isolates the earliest possible nonmonotonicity of expected squared solution error under increasing sampled greediness. It works with an invertible, equal-normalized-row 3 by 3 system on a continuum of initial vectors and strict, tie-free selection, so the reversal is not caused by scale bias, degeneracy, or arbitrary tie-breaking. It distinguishes a natural finite-horizon solver design question from established conditional stepwise progress and rate upper bounds.
